newsitem.title: INDIA: Party critics score a point over India's Rao.
newsitem.headline: Party critics score a point over India's Rao.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao suffered a setback in his Congress party on Tuesday when five of his critics won executive seats in the party's parliamentary group, domestic news agencies said.

"The message of the election is clear and Mr. Rao should step down gracefully (as CPP chief)," Priya Ranjan Das Munshi, one of the five Rao critics elected to the executive, told the Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying.

Rao, who heads the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP), is widely believed to locked into a power battle with Congress president Sitaram Kesri, who took over after Rao quit as party chief in September.

Rao resigned as party president after a court summoned him to testify in a criminal case. But he stayed on as the CPP's chief. The CPP then held elections for its 16-member executive body in the lower house, the Lok Sabha.
Rao has commanded near-unanimous support of the CPP for five years since 1991, when he assumed office as prime minister.

His Congress party suffered its worst electoral humiliation in general elections held this year, but Rao is still seen as influential because his parliamentary group offers make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition.
The electoral defeat and a string of corruption cases involving Rao or his aides have been seen as damaging his popularity across the nation and within his own party.
Kesri has not asked Rao to resign as CPP leader, but has removed some of his loyalists from key party posts in a move seen as a signal for Rao to give up the CPP leader's post.
